items.title: Incorporate the upstream simultaneity update
items.reason: Replace two paragraphs with exact wording from the pinned CC BY upstream and remove the intervening paragraph, as upstream did. No additional prose editing.

changes.before_xml: <ns0:para xmlns:ns0="http://cnx.rice.edu/cnxml" id="import-auto-id2988234">Now suppose we use this method to measure the time interval between two flashes of light produced by flash lamps. (See <ns0:link target-id="import-auto-id3164999" />.) Two flash lamps with observer A midway between them are on a rail car that moves to the right relative to observer B. Observer B arranges for the light flashes to be emitted just as A passes B, so that both A and B are equidistant from the lamps when the light is emitted. Observer B measures the time interval between the arrival of the light flashes. According to postulate 2, the speed of light is not affected by the motion of the lamps relative to B. Therefore, light travels equal distances to him at equal speeds. Thus observer B measures the flashes to be simultaneous.</ns0:para>
changes.after_xml: <ns0:para xmlns:ns0="http://cnx.rice.edu/cnxml" id="import-auto-id2988234">Now suppose we use this method to measure the time interval between two flashes of light produced by flash lamps. (See <ns0:link target-id="import-auto-id3164999" />.) Two flash lamps with observer A midway between them are on a rail car that moves to the right relative to observer B. Observer B arranges for the light flashes to be emitted just as A passes B, so that in B’s frame, both A and B are equidistant from the lamps when the light is emitted. Observer B measures the time interval between the arrival of the light flashes. According to postulate 2, the speed of light is not affected by the motion of the lamps relative to B. Therefore, light travels equal distances to him at equal speeds. Thus, observer B measures the flashes to be simultaneous.  Since in B’s frame, A is moving to the right, B will measure the light from the right bulb and arrive at observer A before the light from the left bulb arrives at observer A.</ns0:para>

changes.before_xml: <ns0:para xmlns:ns0="http://cnx.rice.edu/cnxml" xmlns:ns1="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" id="import-auto-id2693622">Now consider what observer B sees happen to observer A.  Observer B views light from the right reaching observer A before light from the left, because she has moved toward that flash lamp, lessening the distance the light must travel and reducing the time it takes to get to her. Light travels at speed <ns1:math><ns1:semantics><ns1:mrow><ns1:mrow><ns1:mi>c</ns1:mi></ns1:mrow><ns1:mrow /></ns1:mrow><ns1:annotation encoding="StarMath 5.0"> size 12{c} {}</ns1:annotation></ns1:semantics></ns1:math> relative to both observers, but observer B remains equidistant between the points where the flashes were emitted, while A gets closer to the emission point on the right. From observer B’s point of view, then, there is a time interval between the arrival of the flashes to observer A. Observer B measures the flashes to arrive simultaneously relative to him but not relative to A. </ns0:para>
changes.reason: Upstream folds this explanation into the preceding paragraph. Preserve its public anchor if applied.

changes.before_xml: <ns0:para xmlns:ns0="http://cnx.rice.edu/cnxml" id="eip-745">Now consider what observer A sees happening. She sees the light from the right at the same time that she sees the light from the left. Since both lamps are the same distance from her in her reference frame, from her perspective, the flashes occurred at the same time. Here a relative velocity between observers affects whether two events are observed to be simultaneous. <ns0:emphasis effect="italics"><ns0:emphasis effect="italics">Simultaneity is not absolute</ns0:emphasis></ns0:emphasis></ns0:para>
changes.after_xml: <ns0:para xmlns:ns0="http://cnx.rice.edu/cnxml" id="eip-745">Now consider what observer A sees happening. Since both lamps are the same distance from her in her reference frame and the train is moving to the right, she perceives the flash from the right-hand bulb occurring before the left-hand bulb.  Since in her frame, the flashes are not emitted at the same time, they also do not arrive at the same time. Here, a relative velocity between observers affects whether two events are observed to be simultaneous. <ns0:emphasis effect="italics">Simultaneity is not absolute.</ns0:emphasis>. Note, however, that both A and B agree on the order of the flashes arriving at A’s location.</ns0:para>

unchanged: Figure artwork, caption, and image description
upstream_wording_notes: The upstream wording contains “and arrive” and a doubled period after “Simultaneity is not absolute.” These are reproduced without editorial cleanup.
The broader rewrite previously proposed is withdrawn; see Git commit 2ad02f9 for that superseded proposal.
